 03. 1.

entities.text: High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. At the instance of the opposite party no.2, the F.I.R., i.e., Begunia P.S. Case No.189 of 2020 came to be registered against the petitioner under Sections 376(2)(n)/294/506/507/323/34 of the IPC read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act and Section 3(1)(r)(s)/3(2)(va) of the S.C. & S.T. (PoA) Act pending in the Court of POCSO, Bhubaneswar.

3. When the matter was taken up on 22.08.2024, the following order was passed:
"1. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned counsel for the State and learned counsel for the opposite party no.2.
2. The opposite party no.2 appeared in person before this Court along with her Counsel and she is being identified by her Counsel.
She filed her self attested photocopy of the Adhar Card, which is taken on record.
She has also filed an affidavit dated 22.08.2024, inter alia, stating that she has already married elsewhere and blessed with a daughter.
Therefore, she is not willing to prosecute the present petitioner.
The affidavit is taken on record.

3. Mr. Ragada, learned Additional Government Advocate submits that the petitioner has been absconding, who is an accused in Begunia P.S. Case No.189 of 2020 wherein the offence under Section 6 of the POCSO Act and offences under S.C. & S.T. (PoA)
Act are involved apart from panel offences.

4. List this matter on 13th of September, 2023.

Appearance of the opposite party no.2 is not required on the next date."
4.

Mr. Ragada, learned Additional Government Advocate submits that the I.I.C., Begunia Police Station has also verified the fact that the victim has already married to one Santosh Kumar Debata in the year 2023 and at present, she is not interested to proceed with the prosecution against the petitioner.
The victim has also filed an affidavit before this Court to that effect on 22.08.2024 reiterating the aforementioned fact.
So as to save her marital life, she wants to put a quietus to the entire issue.
She apprehends that if this case would go on, her marital life may be jeopardized.
Hence, she is seeking quashing of the entire prosecution case.
5. Taking into consideration the aforementioned facts and the opposite party no.2 is not willing to proceed against the petitioner.

Therefore, the present petition is squarely covered by the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and another reported in 2012 (10) SCC 303 and B.S. Joshi & others vs. State of Haryana & another reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675,

entities.text: B.S. Joshi & others vs. State of Haryana & another reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since subjecting the petitioner to trial will be a futile exercise, I am inclined to quash the criminal proceeding.
6. Regard being had to the aforementioned facts of the case and submission made at bar, Begunia P.S. Case No.189 of 2020 corresponding to T.R. Case No.392 of 2020 pending in the Court of POCSO, Bhubaneswar and the consequential proceedings arising there from qua the petitioner are quashed.
7. The CRLMC is accordingly disposed of.
(S.S. Mishra) Judge amit Location: HIGH COURT OF ORISSA, CUTTACK Purastama Dalei vs State Of Odisha & Another .... Opp. ...
